claim: Scenario work changes expert judgments in the direction the scenario implies (useful items rated more favourably, wasteful less), in field pre/post designs without controls.
agent_test: Run an agent with and without a one-scenario pass on investment items; check shift direction vs scenario usefulness at equal tokens.

claim: Single-scenario and multi-scenario passes change 55-71% of expert judgments but do not change mean confidence (0.811 vs 0.814, p=0.979; chi2 p=0.13).
agent_test: Measure confidence calibration (Brier) before and after a scenario pass at equal tokens.

claim: Highly confident experts change judgments less (about 36% vs about 70%), so scenarios add little where prior confidence is highest.
agent_test: Check whether agent revises high-confidence answers less after scenario prompts.

claim: Multi-scenario exposure shifts experts toward flexible options (Option 1 65.2% to 50.1%; Option 3 12.3% to 23.1%, p<0.001; Option 4 7.4% to 11.4%, p=0.056).
agent_test: Offer an agent flexible vs committed options; measure choice shift after generating several scenarios.

claim: Earlier lab studies disagree on confidence: MBA students widened ranges (Schoemaker 1993), undergraduates grew more confident (Kuhn & Sniezek 1996). Known only via Phadnis summary.
agent_test: Replicate with an LLM: scenario pass vs none, measure interval width and hit rate.

claim: No controlled evidence shows scenario planning improves firm performance. Generic strategic planning correlates modestly (r=.229, 87 correlations, 31 studies, I2=92%, publication-bias tests disagree). Corporate foresight maturity predicts later industry-relative performance in 83 firms (63% vs 24% share of vigilant firms among out- vs underperformers) but in the 2008 cross-section the sign reversed. Phelps 2001 and Zanin 2021 remain weak or unread.
agent_test: Adopt the scenario operator only if it beats a no-scenario arm on a held-out set.

claim: The 68% adoption figure (Diffenbach 1983) is known only through Wikipedia; the paper's existence is confirmed by a catalogue record but its text was not obtained. Klein and Linneman report about 150 of the Fortune 1000 using multiple scenarios (snippet) with loose procedure.
agent_test: Locate the original survey.

claim: Generic strategic planning shows a positive, small-to-moderate performance association: r=.229 (95% CI .186-.271; 87 correlations, 31 studies); r=.255 with one effect per study; I2 about 92%; Egger test signals publication bias; effects smaller with multiple data sources.
agent_test: Not testable on agent.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Fully prospective test: frontier LLMs (Gemini 2.5 Pro rho=0.74; GPT-5 family 0.67-0.71) ranked 30 ventures better than experts (best 0.45, worst 0.04) and Prolific managers (0.19); gap to best expert p=0.063.
agent_test: Compare scaffold vs plain model on prospective ranking tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Prolific crowd ranking had low correlation (0.19) yet captured 85% of oracle value, so rank correlation and value capture can diverge.
agent_test: Report both metrics when testing.

claim: LLM forecasting: best plain model Brier 0.208, retrieval-augmented system 0.179, human crowd 0.149, random 0.250; accuracy 71.5% vs 77.0%.
agent_test: Equal-token forecasting with and without retrieval.

claim: LLM forecasters match or beat crowds only in some settings; combining LLM and human median improves accuracy (17-28% gains).
agent_test: Ensemble scaffold output with a simple prior at equal tokens.

claim: Prompt-level reflection reduces LLM escalation in wargames: planning prompt -28%, de-escalation reflection -57%, temperature 0.01 -48% (10 runs per treatment).
agent_test: Reproduce on a non-wargame scenario task.

claim: LLM wargame behaviour differs from human experts, resists instruction (GPT-4 matched human frequency on 10 of 21 actions) and is unstable (>50% score swings in one turn).
agent_test: Run repeated seeds, report variance.

claim: LLM advice varies by country named (less escalation advised for China/Russia than US/UK), a bias risk in scenario generation.
agent_test: Swap actor names in scenario prompts and compare outputs.

claim: Sampling more candidate futures or decisions helps in places: DeLLMa up to +40% accuracy with test-time scaling; PlanRAG +15.8%/+7.4%; K-Level gains, but K=3 lowered win rate in one game.
agent_test: Vary number of scenarios 1-8 at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs rarely recognise the strategic structure of a business task unprompted: best model passes the gate on 27.9% of 223 tasks; top two overlap 31.7%.
agent_test: Test a problem-recognition step before scenarios.

claim: In a business simulation LLM agents vary 9.0x in net worth, 51% of runs lose money, best expert strategy exceeds 2x best model mean.
agent_test: Run scaffold on a simulated market at equal tokens.

claim: Single prompts give low diversity; stratification or targeted prompting raises coverage (SimpleStrat recall +0.05; diverse-perspective recall 37.5% on one set).
agent_test: Measure scenario diversity with embeddings or a judge at equal tokens.

claim: There are no controlled studies of LLM-generated scenarios improving decision quality. Spaniol and Rowland (2023) is opinion without measurements; Kozachek 2026 and the Time Machine study could not be read (snippets only).
agent_test: Build the first one: scenario operator vs none.

claim: Pre/post mental-model change after scenario planning in 129 participants (no control). The AI-augmented foresight experiment (Kanis et al. 2026, N=348, 2x2) is a startup-evaluation task: LLM use raised breadth, lowered depth and consensus, left foresight accuracy unchanged (abstract only, no effect sizes).
agent_test: Verify the Strategy Science paper before relying on it.

claim: A one-prompt scenario step does not improve LLM forecast calibration: Hypothetical Scenario Analysis -0.007 Brier vs control (p=.411, adjusted .774) and Premortem -0.008 (adjusted .774) across 100 questions and 4 models; scenario combinations in Study 2 -0.001 to +0.004 (adjusted p .79-.985). Base-rate prompts did help (adjusted significant) and Bayesian-reasoning prompts hurt.
agent_test: Equal-token arms: no scenario, base rate first, base rate then scenario; compare Brier and 80% interval hit rate on resolved questions.

claim: Where scenario use is controlled in humans, the one verified design shows reduced framing bias and better decision quality versus traditional tools (Meissner and Wulf 2013, 252 graduate students), but only the abstract was read and the bias is framing, not anchoring.
agent_test: Give gain-frame and loss-frame versions of the same decision; check answers agree with and without a scenario pass.

claim: Self-reported planning benefits shrink when performance data come from a source independent of the survey (common-source bias in George et al. 2019), and the 2008 cross-sectional foresight link was reversed in Rohrbeck and Kum, so time lag and rater matter.
agent_test: Grade scenario benefit with an outside grader or resolved outcomes, never the agent's own rating.

claim: LLM breadth aids (more scenarios, more perspectives) can widen representations without improving accuracy and lower consensus (Kanis 2026 abstract; Schoenegger 2025 prompts); a convergence step is needed.
agent_test: Measure option breadth and final accuracy together; check breadth gain converts to better final choice.

claim: Open after gap search: no measured implementation-rate effect of scenarios (de Geus follow-through), no experiment varying number of scenarios, no scaffold test of actor-name bias, no numbers on LLM vs human scenario diversity (Kozachek 2026 unread).
agent_test: Run own bench ablations: 2 vs 3 vs 5 scenarios; neutral vs named actors.
